explanation: The I84V mutation reduces the hydrophobic packing density within the S1/S1' subpocket by removing approximately 27 Å³ of van der Waals contact surface, weakening the favorable binding interactions that saquinavir's inhibitor scaffold normally makes with the protease core. Although the mutation introduces minimal perturbation at long range (>10 Å from ligand center), the direct contact at 3.3 Å indicates that the smaller valine side chain creates a cavity defect that destabilizes the precise shape complementarity saquinavir requires for optimal occupancy of this critical substrate-binding site. The loss of marginal hydrophobic interactions—without compensatory gains from charge rearrangement or new contacts—translates to the modest but measurable decrease in binding free energy.
